native_routines_run: 0x18dde70 contact-flag refresh (container count loop, payload flag test, link flag set or clear)
method: Refresh 0x18dde70 run natively with the two accessors hooked as recording services that perform the same container reads through unicorn memory. The Python reference refresh_pose_link_contact_flag reads the same fixture through PoseFlatMemory with its own accessors. Callee-saved rbx, rbp and rsi are checked after each native run.
comparisons: accessor call order with arguments (container address, index)
final 0x100-byte link bytes including bit0 of +0x84 and every other flag bit
every payload object byte range (0x200 each)
callee-saved registers rbx, rbp and rsi
coverage: payload flag bit0 set in about 25 percent of entries; other bits of the +0x114 byte are random, so bit1 alone and other bits are present but do not affect the result
link flag +0x84 random before refresh, set and clear paths both exercised
zero payload pointer at a random index in 1 of 16 trials (native and reference both fault)
limits: The two accessors are small leaf reads supplied as services; the harness models them with the container layout read from the nested-object fields, not with their native code.
Payload objects are fixtures of 0x200 bytes; only the +0x114 byte is semantically used.
No live validation, no concurrent flag writers, and no check that the entries at +0x58 belong to a real contact span.
